english: May the brahmacharins come to me — svāhā!
May I move about — svāhā!
May I shine forth — svāhā!
May I be superior in good things — svāhā!
May I move among people as one possessed of glory — svāhā!
May I be dear to the gods, to men, to cattle, to the brahmacharins.
Make me beloved of Prajāpati — svāhā!
O mother, wondrous wanderer!

sanskrit: ayaṃ me hasto akṣito rudati tam u me agadaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: This hand of mine is unimpaired; he weeps — make that one free of disease for me.

sanskrit: tvaṃ kṣitsya bheṣajy ubhayor akṣitasya ca ||
english: You are the remedy of the wasted and of both — of the unimpaired as well.
O Udelaḍi!
You are life-breath — svāhā!
You are will and resolve — svāhā!
You are the person — svāhā!
You are of distinct birth — svāhā!
You are of offspring-birth — svāhā!
You are of your own kind — svāhā!
Your name is 'of your own kind' — svāhā!

sanskrit: veda vai te nārada nāma vāg nāmāsi tasya te yaśo bhakṣīya ||
english: I know your name, O Nārada — you are named Speech; may I partake of your glory.

sanskrit: veda vai te sanāt kumāra nāma cakṣur nāmāsi tasya te madhu bhakṣīya ||
english: I know your name, O Sanatkumāra — you are named Sight; may I partake of your sweetness.

sanskrit: snuṣāsau senāsyāḥ senāyā ihāsyāḥ śvaśuroyam asyāḥ śvaśuraḥ | sā yathā snuṣā śvaśurād adhaspadyate adharā padyate nīcī padyate ||
english: That one is the daughter-in-law of this army, of this army here; this is her father-in-law, her father-in-law. Just as a daughter-in-law falls down before her father-in-law, falls lower, falls down in submission —

sanskrit: evāsau senāsyāḥ senāyā adhas padyatām adharā padyatāṃ nīcī padyatām | sendrāgnibhyāṃ hatavīrāṃ hatapūruṣāṃ parājitāṃ praṇuttaitu paramāṃ parāvatam ||
english: So may that army of his fall down beneath this army, fall lower, fall down in submission. Struck of its heroes, struck of its men, defeated and driven away by Indra and Agni together, may it retreat to the farthest distance.

sanskrit: tām indrāgnī hatavīrāṃ hatapūruṣāṃ parājitāṃ praṇuttāṃ yatīm anvākśītām | parājita etv asāv āmuṣyāyaṇo amuṣyāḥ putraḥ ||
english: May Indra and Agni look upon that army struck of its heroes, struck of its men, defeated, driven away, fleeing. May that son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so, come away defeated.

sanskrit: asnā vyakta etu | aghaṃ hi raṇyetv asāv āmuṣyāyaṇo amuṣyāḥ putraḥ ||
english: May he come away laid bare without flesh. For may that son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so, revel in misfortune.

sanskrit: aghapratīko aghenainaṃ vidhyāmaḥ | abhūtyā enaṃ pāśe sitvā duṣvapnyena saṃ sṛjya mṛtyor vyātta āsann api dadhāmi ||
english: We pierce him with evil — he whose face is evil. Having bound him in the noose of ill-fortune, having united him with evil dreams, I place him into the open mouth of Death.
